classes.name: Elección del Presidente y Vicepresidente de la República
classes.locator: Artículo 124 (elected every four years by direct vote), Artículo 125 (vice president on the same ticket), Artículo 209.1 (runoff on the last Sunday of June when no ticket has more than half the valid votes)
classes.finest_note: 2000-2024: by electoral college in the JCE's xlsx and xls files. 1994-1998: by municipality for each level. 1962-1986: by municipality, one column of party votes for the presidency and one for all other candidacies. 1990: ballots per province and level only.
classes.note: Joint ticket elected by national direct vote. The JCE, created by Ley 35 of 8 March 1923, ran its first presidential election on 15 March 1924; presidents chosen before 1924 under the constitutions of 1844-1908 are not yet researched. The 1994 crisis cut the term elected that year to two years, so presidential elections moved to 1996 and every four years after, apart from the congressional and municipal ones, until 2016. The two-round majority rule dates from the 1994 reform; the only runoff so far was 30 June 1996. The 2020 election, proclaimed for 17 May, was held on 5 July. Votes abroad count since 2004.

classes.note: One senator per province and the Distrito Nacional (32 in 2010, 2016, and 2024), by plurality. Until 2016 the senator and the province's deputies were elected on one congressional ballot. Elections before 1962 are not yet listed from official sources.

classes.name: Concurrencia de las mujeres a manera de ensayo
classes.name_en: Women's trial votes on the constitutional reform
classes.note: Decree 858 of 22 December 1933 let women vote, as a trial, with the 1934 general elections to express support for reforming the articles of the Constitution that disadvantaged them; 96,247 women voted on 16 May 1934, and they did so again in 1938. The 1942 constitutional reform gave women the vote.
classes.disposition_reason: The JCE publishes only the national 1934 turnout (96,247 women) in its history; no count by unit is on its portal.

classes.name: Referendo
classes.locator: Artículo 210 (referendums by law, approved by two thirds of each chamber, never on a mandate) and Artículo 272 (referendo aprobatorio of reforms to rights, territory, nationality, currency, or the reform procedure)
classes.note: The 2010 Constitution introduced national referendums and the referendo aprobatorio; transitional provision Sexta exempted the 2024 reform from it.
classes.disposition_reason: No national referendum has been held: the JCE lists none among its elections, and the only constitutional reform since 2010 subject to the rule (2024) was exempted by transitional provision Sexta.

classes.name: Referendo, plebiscito e iniciativa normativa municipales
classes.locator: Artículo 203: the organic law of local administration sets the scope, requirements, and conditions of municipal referendums, plebiscites, and normative initiatives
classes.disposition_reason: The JCE publishes no municipal referendum or plebiscite results, and whether any has been held is not established from official sources.

classes.name: Elecciones de segundo grado del Senado
classes.locator: Artículo 80.3-5: the Senate elects the Cámara de Cuentas, the members of the Junta Central Electoral, and the Defensor del Pueblo by two thirds; Artículo 77.1: chambers fill their own vacancies from a party's terna
classes.disposition_reason: Appointments voted in the Senate (and vacancy fills in each chamber), recorded only in legislative journals; no electorate votes.
